summary: This note is a collection of facts about the TV singing competition American Idol, covering its seasons, winners, judges, finals format, sponsors, recording deals and cultural impact. It highlights the show's launch in 2002 on Fox, notable contestants and controversies, and its success as a launching pad for recording artists. It also covers side items like Idol Gives Back and Disney's The American Idol Experience.
one_line: Overview of American Idol's seasons, judges, winners, format, sponsors, music industry deals and impact as a launching pad for pop stars.
key_facts: The first season of American Idol debuted as a summer replacement show in June 2002 on Fox, co-hosted by Ryan Seacrest and Brian Dunkleman.

Original judges Randy Jackson, Paula Abdul and Simon Cowell stayed on the panel for eight seasons; planned fourth judge Stryker dropped out citing 'image concerns' and Angie Martinez withdrew in season two.
Billboard said that in its first ten years Idol spawned 345 Billboard chart-toppers; in 2007 Idol alumni accounted for 2.1% of all music sales.
Carrie Underwood won in May 2005, has sold 65 million records worldwide and has won seven Grammy Awards, the most by an Idol alumnus.
Jennifer Hudson, who placed seventh in Fantasia's season, is the only Idol contestant to win both an Academy Award and a Grammy.

Sponsorship deals cost around $10 million in season one, $35 million by season 7, and $50 to $60 million in season 10; Coca-Cola ended its sponsorship after season 13 and AT&T Wireless after season 12.

PepsiCo declined to sponsor Idol at the start, which the Los Angeles Times said was 'missing one of the biggest marketing opportunities in a generation'; Pepsi had fallen to third place in the US by 2010.
Idol Gives Back, a charity event started in season six and also held in seasons seven and nine, raised nearly $185 million in total.
Disney's 'The American Idol Experience' opened February 14, 2009 at Disney's Hollywood Studios and closed August 30, 2014.
Season 12 premiered January 16, 2013 with judges Randy Jackson, Mariah Carey, Keith Urban and Nicki Minaj, and was marked by the Minaj-Carey feud leaked to TMZ.
Kris Allen beat Adam Lambert in season eight in a controversial result, with a claim (later retracted) that 38 million of 100 million votes came from Arkansas.
Sanjaya Malakar was voted off on April 18 in season six after surviving many weeks with support from Vote for the Worst and Howard Stern.
Season 13 was the first season where contestants could perform self-written songs in the finals; Sam Woolf was saved by the judges in the Top 8, and the 500th episode was the Top 3 night.
Nick Fradiani won season 14, becoming the first winner from the Northeast region, defeating Clark Beckham.
The show's recording rights are held by 19 Recordings, with Sony Music distributing until 2010, when UMG's Interscope-Geffen-A&M Records replaced Sony.
